subject: Marketplace Private Offer & Unit Pricing — BrightArc
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nolan <sara@brightarc.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace Private Offer & Unit Pricing — BrightArc

Hi Sara / team,

Thanks again for taking time today — good discussion and appreciate the clarity on your main goals (real-time inference for customer-facing features, predictable cost, and a marketplace procurement path). Quick recap + asks so we can align internal teams and AWS marketplace flow: 

Key takeaways from call:
- Target workload: conversational traffic ~20–50M tokens/month initially, with burst windows up to ~200M tokens in peak months.
- Target procurement: prefer AWS Marketplace Private Offer so finance can route a PO; customer would like to map to a single $/1M tokens unit for SaaS consumption.
- Timing: procurement review starts 3/15; goal to have pricing and PO draft by 3/22.

Immediate asks (what we need from BrightArc):
1) Confirm target committed baseline (conservative) for private offer (e.g., 20M/mo vs 50M/mo).
2) Confirm target net unit economics — you mentioned a target in the ~$150–200 per 1M tokens range; confirm if $/1M is net to Redwood (post-marketplace fees) or gross.
3) Any required legal flow for PO/terms? Who is the finance contact?

What we’ll deliver by 3/10:
- An initial unit-price mapping spreadsheet showing: Redwood list price, marketplace gross price (to account for AWS fee), and the net revenue to Redwood at different marketplace fee rates. See attached workbook (BrightArc_token_modeling_v2.xlsx).
- A proposed Private Offer template (will use AWS Marketplace flow) and an internal summary of discounts required for committed volumes.

Next steps: Aditya will run a price-mapping with marketplace fee assumptions (AWS takes a percentage on gross in the purchase flow); we’ll send a recommended gross price to list in the Private Offer that hits your target net $/1M. Rishi, would you be able to confirm finance approval window for a potential one-time onboarding credit?

Thanks — I’ll loop in AWS marketplace contacts if needed once we have the confirmed baseline.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0117

Subject: Re: Marketplace Private Offer & Unit Pricing — BrightArc

Marissa,

Thanks — all sounds good. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Committed baseline: BrightArc is leaning to start at 30M tokens/month for the private offer (we can consider ramp credits for months 1–3).
- Target unit: Our procurement folks want to budget against one line item: $/1M tokens. Finance indicated an internal target of $180 per 1M tokens (this would be the number they expect to be charged on their PO).
- Marketplace flow: finance will prefer the AWS Private Offer so costs hit our existing cloud budget. Our finance contact is Ben Carter (ben@brightarc.com). Ben will expect the PO to reference the HubSpot deal id we shared.

Question: when you say "net to Redwood" vs "gross on Marketplace" — we expect the $180 to be the gross charge on the AWS invoice (i.e., what AWS bills us). If we need a higher gross to cover marketplace fees and still hit a target payout to Redwood, please show both numbers in your mapping.

Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Sara Nolan
Head of Product | BrightArc

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nolan <sara@brightarc.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Marketplace Private Offer & Unit Pricing — BrightArc

Hi Sara — quick pricing note / math so everyone has the mapping. I updated the attached workbook with worked examples. Highlights: 

Assumptions we used in the sheet: 
- Customer target (gross on AWS invoice): $180 per 1M tokens (per Sara).
- Marketplace fee model (example): AWS Marketplace takes 20% of gross purchase as a fee in some deals (this varies by agreement; could be 10–25%).
- Redwood target net revenue per 1M tokens: we model $150 net to Redwood (this is illustrative).

Mappings and formula: 
- If marketplace fee = 20%, gross_on_aws = net_to_redwood / (1 - fee_rate). So to deliver $150 net, gross = 150 / 0.8 = $187.50.
- If customer insists on $180 gross on invoice, Redwood net = 180 * (1 - 0.2) = $144.00. That would be below the $150 illustrative target.

Options to reconcile: 
1) Increase gross price listed on the Private Offer so AWS invoice is $187.50 (Redwood nets $150). Need to validate with BrightArc whether their finance can accept that number on their AWS invoice.
2) Redwood accept a slightly lower net (e.g., $144) in exchange for a 12-month commitment and reserved capacity. We modeled a 10% concession for 12-months in the workbook.
3) Use an onboarding credit (one-time) to bridge the delta for first 3 months.

Examples in the workbook (tab: "Marketplace Mapping"): price rows for 20M, 30M, 50M committed baselines and effective $/1M after discounting. Also included a column showing our recommended gross price to list in the Private Offer for each net target.

Next steps I propose (timeline): 
- Today/3/3: Aditya to finalize recommended gross price table and attach the private offer template.
- By 3/10: Marissa to confirm BrightArc accepts gross listed price or pick a concession option.
- By 3/15: If accepted, we generate AWS Private Offer draft and route to Ben at BrightArc for PO signature.

Short note on fees: Marketplace fee rates can vary by channel (AWS, GCP, Azure). Our model in the workbook makes the fee rate a parameter so we can quickly show mappings for different marketplace fee assumptions.

Attachments: BrightArc_token_modeling_v2.xlsx, aws_private_offer_template.docx

—Aditya

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-03T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Marketplace Private Offer & Unit Pricing — BrightArc

Looping in briefly from finance/ops perspective — thanks for the clear mapping. Two internal asks before we finalize: 
1) Marissa — can you confirm whether the proposed private offer will include a 12-month commitment term? If yes, finance is prepared to approve a 10% concession on Redwood net list price but needs that commitment and a signed PO.
2) Aditya — please add a short summary tab in the workbook that calls out the exact AWS gross to list per 1M token for each commit tier (20/30/50M). Keep the marketplace fee as an editable cell.

Sara — if BrightArc is flexible on gross_to_aws = $187.50 for the $150 net case, finance expects that we can proceed with standard private-offer routing. If not, we’ll need a short note from Ben (finance) confirming they require $180 on invoice and accept that Redwood nets the lower amount.

I’ll standby to route the internal discount approval once we have the confirmed commit term and the PO flow.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
